A few generated candidates are ranked by a learned critic, and the model-based MPC then enforces dynamics and constraints. In a kinematic overtaking benchmark derived from ZipMPC, more than half of the contexts are bimodal and the manual short-horizon MPC crashes in 28% of them. With an eight-dimensional stagewise correction, evaluated on 1000 fresh contexts and five training seeds, ZipDrift with eight candidates crashes in 0.74% of episodes, compared with 3.4% for an idealised ZipMPC-style regressor and 2.1% for critic-ranked random candidates with the same budget. A mixture density network (MDN) with the same selection is equally good (0.76%). The benefit of drifting lies in sample quality: in a pre-specified test on further unseen contexts, a single drifting sample crashes in 8.7% of episodes against 13.2% for the MDN, and ZipDrift needs four candidates instead of eight to fall below 1%. With many candidates, all methods degrade as selection exploits errors of the critic.

papers.title: The Male Abstraction Bias in Internet Culture and Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Conceptual abstraction and gender are two equally central aspects of the human mind, yet they have traditionally been studied in isolation from one another, as though they were fundamentally separate. Here, we find gender and abstraction are systematically linked throughout the space of concepts spanning single (N = 40,000) and multi-word expressions (N = 67,000): across billions of words and millions of images on the internet --- and across numerous measurement techniques, including human and AI classifications --- more abstract concepts are more associated with men, a pattern we show replicates in languages around the world. This male abstraction bias not only holds across semantic domains, but it also maps onto grammatical structure: verbs and adverbs are more abstract and more male-coded, revealing a system-wide trace of stereotypes accentuating agentic qualities in men. Furthermore, we show this bias readily emerges in the free associations humans and AIs produce in controlled online tasks, indicating its psychological internalization and its algorithmic reproduction. These findings identify a latent structure in conceptual space that unifies a range of stereotypes: for example, framings of women as more embodied, emotional, and warm, versus men as more cognitive, rational, and competent; as well as erroneous views of men as better at mathematics, science, and engineering. More broadly, by analyzing an unprecedentedly large, multimodal sample of online data, we provide culture-wide evidence of gender as a core organizing principle shaping conceptual space far beyond the characterization of people and social roles.

papers.title: FRESHPart: Feedback-Reshaped Spectral Embedding for Hypergraph Partitioning
papers.abstract: With scalable Laplacian solvers now available, the next frontier is to exploit them more effectively for high-quality hypergraph partitioning. In this work, we revisit spectral hypergraph partitioning from the perspective of spectral embedding geometry. Through a systematic analysis of circuit hypergraphs and controlled synthetic (hyper)graphs, we identify a ray-like embedding structure that helps explain the effectiveness of projection-based partitioning. We further show that the geometry of spectral embeddings can be systematically influenced through Laplacian design and hyperedge reweighting. Guided by these insights, we propose FRESHPart, a feedback-reshaped spectral partitioning framework that refines the spectral embedding through Geometry Feedback and Search Feedback, producing embeddings that are better aligned with projection-based partitioning. On the Titan23 benchmark, FRESHPart achieves average cut reductions over hMETIS of 13.09% at $\epsilon=2\%$ and 25.21% at $\epsilon=20\%$, surpassing the strongest previously reported results (12.16% and 22.53%, respectively), while completing every benchmark in under 120 s on a single GPU.

papers.title: The potential impact of fiscal rule changes on digital products trade
papers.abstract: The WTO moratorium on customs duties on electronic transmissions lapsed in March 2026, allowing governments to impose tariffs on cross-border digital products, alongside other instruments such as digital services taxes (DSTs). Yet, how tariffs and DSTs compare in the revenue they raise and their effect on trade in digital products has not yet been assessed. Here we combine bilateral trade in 31 digital product categories in 2016-2024 with DST rates and tariffs on physical analogues, estimate gravity models and simulate alternative fiscal regimes. We find that digital trade is lower in destinations with a DST, but within destinations it declines only temporarily after adoption. In conditional scenarios for 2024 based on the event study estimate, adding tariff equivalents to DSTs raises revenue from USD 2.7 to 6.9 billion and lowers trade by about 1.4%, and replacing DSTs with tariff equivalents raises USD 4.3 billion. We also find that tariff-equivalent payments are attributed mainly to the United States and DST payments to subsidiary locations such as Ireland. In sum, these results suggest that tariffs on digital products could raise more revenue than DSTs at a modest cost in trade.

papers.title: Economic Policy Uncertainty Index for Poland: Data, Construction, and Validation
papers.abstract: We construct a continuous monthly Economic Policy Uncertainty (EPU) index for Poland spanning January 2000 to June 2026, following the newspaper-based Baker-Bloom-Davis (BBD) methodology. The index uses six deep-history Polish newspapers (Rzeczpospolita, Parkiet, Gazeta Wyborcza, Dziennik Gazeta Prawna, Gazeta Polska Codziennie, and Puls Biznesu), scaled by article volume, standardized to unit standard deviation over a fixed 2000-2024 baseline (300 months), averaged across available papers each period, and normalized so the baseline mean equals 100. Because newspapers enter the panel at different dates, a naive expanding-panel average can jump at each entry point from a change in composition rather than real uncertainty. We correct for this using the BBD Appendix A splicing procedure: a backward chain-splice from the richest six-paper anchor panel that matches dispersion via a multiplicative scale factor and matches level via a multiplicative ratio over each overlap window, yielding an index that is level-continuous across all entry points. The index rises sharply during the COVID-19 lockdown, the 2022 energy crisis, and the 2023 change of government, with its largest reaction following the 2016 Brexit referendum -- an external event with major implications for Poland's economic-policy environment. In month-on-month changes, Poland's EPU is moderately correlated with the US (0.26) and global (0.25) EPU indices. Together with the event-based evidence, these modest correlations support our central finding: EPU Index PL captures economic policy uncertainty that is predominantly domestic, driven mainly by developments in Poland's own economic policy rather than merely international spillovers, though international shocks remain relevant insofar as they create uncertainty about Poland's own policy decisions.

papers.title: Contextual Pictograms for Repairing Multilingual ASR Errors
papers.abstract: Speech transcription errors can be difficult to recognize when competing word hypotheses are unfamiliar or visually similar. We describe an interface that combines alternative transcripts, replay and contextually checked pictograms for selected uncertain concepts. The system will initially support French and Spanish functional utterances. A counterbalanced study will assess whether pictorial feedback helps listeners recover the speaker's intended action beyond text alternatives alone. We will also quantify semantic mismatch and additional interaction time, since an inappropriate image can reinforce the wrong interpretation rather than repair it.

papers.title: Whiel: A Neurosymbolic Platform for Certified Relational Program Verification
papers.abstract: We present the Whiel (a contraction of Whi(le-R)el) system for Lean-certified reasoning about imperative relational programs. The system can encode containment and equivalence problems for Datalog, its extensions with negation, and the core fragment of graph query languages. It can also represent optimized or incremental evaluation algorithms that are not expressible in the original query language, as well as first-order specifications of integrity constraints, schema mappings, and views arising in data integration, exchange, and sharing. Whiel's program states are database instances, and its imperative structure enables compositional Hoare-style reasoning with first-order relational specifications, using prophecy variables and leveled invariants to support inductive arguments. Whiel supports neurosymbolic discovery of loop invariants whose verification conditions can be checked using the Vampire first-order theorem prover. Counterexamples are fed back into the neurosymbolic pipeline, while proposed solutions are translated into Lean proof certificates. To validate the Whiel system, we evaluate its performance on a curated benchmark suite. In summary, we envision the Whiel system as a tool for tackling mathematically demanding, typically undecidable problems involving complex query and constraint languages, with a high degree of trust in its output.

papers.title: Distinguishing Initial-Condition and Model Error Using Machine-Learning Weather Models
papers.abstract: Differentiable weather models allow atmospheric initial conditions to be directly optimized to shadow a known trajectory, which we take from a reanalysis dataset. Here, we extend this optimization to include the forecast model, GraphCast, using low-rank adaptation (LoRA). We compare model optimization with initial-condition (IC) optimization, and then joint optimization, where both are tuned simultaneously. When compared against a control forecast initialized with reanalysis data, LoRA and IC optimization individually produce similar improvements. We find similar results when IC and LoRA are jointly optimized across a spectrum of solutions where a tuning coefficient smoothly shifts the weight of the joint optimization from all-LoRA to all-IC; forecast improvement is not unique to the relative contributions of model and IC corrections. To better discriminate the source of error, we introduce a second model, Pangu-Weather, as a supervisor that gates IC updates during joint optimization. This gated optimization is the same as before, except that IC updates at each epoch are accepted only when they improve the forecasts of both models; otherwise, only the LoRA update is accepted. Results show that this cross-model constraint substantially improves agreement between the two models in their response to the same optimized ICs, narrowing the gap in mean forecast error reduction from 64% to 10%. Moreover, when used together, the LoRA and IC corrections from the gated optimization yield GraphCast forecast improvements similar to those from the ungated optimization. These results imply that model error that is encoded in the ungated ICs is shifted to the LoRA corrections via gating, yielding IC corrections that may provide better analysis estimates.

papers.title: Whose Values Are Generated? Measuring Visual Value Leakage in Multilingual Text-to-Image Generation
papers.abstract: Text-to-image (T2I) systems serve users across languages and cultural contexts. However, evaluations of cultural representation focus mainly on recognizable elements such as landmarks, clothing, and activities, overlooking the cultural values that generated images convey. To bridge this gap, we introduce VisionValueBench, a multilingual benchmark that operationalizes six of Hofstede's cultural value dimensions (e.g., individualism versus collectivism) to investigate how T2I systems frame neutral social situations through a particular cultural orientation. We find that value-neutral prompts, which admit diverse cultural interpretations, nonetheless yield images that favor particular value orientations, a phenomenon we call visual value leakage. We evaluate prompts varying in language and geographic cues across 960 social scenarios and six T2I configurations. Generated images consistently favor the same value orientations across all six dimensions, for example, equality over hierarchy (low power distance), individual autonomy over group obligation (individualism), and enjoyment over restraint (indulgence). Prompt language has limited influence on these orientations, whereas geographic cues shift some dimensions toward the associated cultural values while largely preserving the prevailing orientations. These findings reveal substantial homogeneity in the cultural values conveyed by T2I systems worldwide.

papers.title: Decision Models as Scalable Economic Surrogates that Capture Human Variation
papers.abstract: Decision Models (DMs), a new class of AI models, give fast responses and return a probability distribution over a fixed set of options. These properties make them candidate human surrogates in economic simulations and surveys, a role increasingly filled by Large Language Models (LLMs), which are costly at scale and under-represent the variation in human behaviour. We present a first evaluation of DMs as human surrogates in economics, comparing 10 DMs with 8 LLMs in three economic settings: a household spending survey on consumption, several classic economic games and a labour-market field experiment. Frontier DMs, those that score highest on general decision-making benchmarks, reproduce the variation in human responses more closely than LLMs in all three settings. They capture the modal human response as well as LLMs in the spending survey, but less well in the economic games. Frontier DMs are also roughly ten times faster than the fastest LLM and can be over a hundred times cheaper. Together, these results suggest that DMs capture the heterogeneity of human behaviour better than LLMs and make large-scale economic simulations more feasible.

papers.title: Data-Driven Stochastic LQR Control with Probabilistic Guarantees and Uncertainty Refinement
papers.abstract: This paper presents a probabilistic framework for the direct, data-driven synthesis of the stochastic linear- quadratic output-feedback control for linear systems sub- ject to process and measurement noise. Using delayed input-output measurements, we derive a lifted parameter- ization together with an equivalent lifted linear quadratic cost, enabling controller synthesis without explicitly identi- fying the lifted dynamics. Two complementary closed-loop formulations, based on trajectory and covariance represen- tations, are then developed, whose uncertainties depend only on the realized but unknown lifted noise. We char- acterize the relative performance of the two formulations in finite-data regimes. High-probability uncertainty bounds are developed for realized noises, leading to a convex optimization solution to the problem, whose feasibility cer- tifies probabilistic mean-square stability (p-MSS) and per- formance guarantees. To reduce conservatism, Gaussian zonotopes are used to refine uncertainty sets by elimi- nating noise realizations inconsistent with measured data, and a novel intersection rule enables the consistent fusion of data-driven and physics-informed information. These components are integrated into an adaptive framework that unifies indirect (identification-based) and direct (control- oriented) data-driven linear-quadratic output-feedback con- trol. Unlike existing direct data-driven LQR methods that verify stability a posteriori, our by-construction approach achieves robust stability alongside reduced conservatism and superior performance. Simulation results show that the proposed controller approaches the ideal optimal solution while outperforming existing data-driven methods under noisy measurements.

papers.title: LIBRA: Programmatic Induction of Executable Tool Libraries
papers.abstract: Large language model agents increasingly retrieve tools from large catalogs, yet most retrievers rank each tool independently by request similarity. For multi tool tasks, this recovers the goal matching tool while omitting prerequisite tools required by the workflow. We introduce LIBRA, a framework for Library Induction by Runtime Assembly that turns a flat tool catalog into an executable tool library. An LLM proposes per tool contracts of candidate invocations, reusable outputs and state changes, and success conditions; LIBRA then tests these compositions in a sandbox and retains the relations supported at runtime. Constructed before user queries, the library requires no dependency annotations, tool use trajectories, or task specific training, and supports both one-shot and agentic retrieval. On AppWorld, BFCL, and SciToolEval, LIBRA improves one-shot Recall and NDCG over the same dense retriever by 7.9 and 3.7 percentage points on average. Within ToolReAGt, it yields corresponding gains of 4.5 and 2.9 points after ten retrieval iterations.

papers.title: Isosceles sets and two-distance sets in Euclidean space
papers.abstract: A finite set of points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is isosceles if every three of its points form an isosceles triangle. Erd\H{o}s asked in 1946 for the largest size $\mathrm{iso}(d)$ of an isosceles set in $\mathbb{R}^d$; the answer was known for $d\le8$. Let $g(d)$ and $M(d)$ be the largest sizes of a two-distance set and of a spherical two-distance set in $\mathbb{R}^d$. We prove that $\mathrm{iso}(d)=\max\{g(d),M(d)+1,M(d-1)+3\}$ for every $d\ge2$, which reduces the problem to these two classical ones. With the recently determined values of $g(d)$ for $9\le d\le22$ we obtain $\mathrm{iso}(d)=\binom{d+1}{2}+1$ for $9\le d\le21$ and $\mathrm{iso}(22)=276$, and we show that the extremal set is unique: for $d\le21$ it is the set of midpoints of the edges of a regular simplex together with its centroid, and for $d=22$ it is the McLaughlin configuration together with its centre. For $10\le d\le22$ every isosceles set with more than $\binom d2+3$ points is a two-distance set or a spherical two-distance set together with its centre. The proofs start from Blokhuis' decomposition of isosceles sets into mutually orthogonal two-distance sets. Counting leaves one configuration open: a two-distance set with $\binom{d+1}{2}$ points in a hyperplane, the largest number allowed by Blokhuis' bound, together with two points that are mirror images of each other. We exclude it by showing that a two-distance set $T$ attaining Blokhuis' bound in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is unisolvent for quadratic polynomials and that, if $T$ lies on two concentric spheres, then apart from two exceptional cases its two layers are spherical $2$-designs whose sizes are determined by the radii. We also show that the squared distances of such a set are in ratio $(k-1):k$ with $(2k-1)^2\le n+1$ if $n\ge9$. Hence there is none for $9\le n\le23$, so that $g(23)\le299$ and $\mathrm{iso}(23)=\max\{g(23),278\}\le299$.

papers.title: A normalization issue in a transmitted form of Bloch's diamond formula: anti-invariant subgroup versus regulator quotient
papers.abstract: Bloch's regulator formula for an elliptic curve is often quoted with a generator of the anti-invariant subgroup $H_1(E,\mathbb{Z})^-$ and coefficient $1$ in front of the elliptic dilogarithm of the diamond product. We compare this wording with Brunault's published intersection-product formula. The natural map from the anti-invariant subgroup to the regulator quotient $H_1(E,\mathbb{Z})/H_1(E,\mathbb{Z})^+$ has index $1$ when $E(\mathbb{R})$ has two components and index $2$ when it has one. Thus, up to orientation, the coefficient is $1$ for a quotient generator and $\iota(E)\in\{1,2\}$ for a subgroup generator. This is an elementary consequence of the published formula, not a new regulator theorem. We illustrate the distinction on 11.a3 using an externally proved regulator anchor and the Brunault--Bertin special values, and on 20.a4 by high-precision numerical integration. We also correct our earlier quotation of Touafek: his printed identity is $\pi r=D_E((f)\diamond(g))$, with $r=(2\pi)^{-1}\int_{\gamma^-}\eta$. It is compatible with the subgroup normalization when $\Delta 0$ the corresponding coefficient is $1/2$, up to orientation. We do not reassess his isogeny theorem or his final exotic relation here. No new proof of Boyd's conductor-11 split-integral identity is included.

papers.title: BIOTRAM: Biochemistry-informed Transformer for Relative Abundance via Metabarcoding
papers.abstract: Arthropod monitoring at scale begins with metabarcoding of bulk samples: trap collections of hundreds to thousands of specimens processed as one unit, extraction of DNA from the bulked specimens, then sequencing of the DNA from all specimens together. Metabarcoding reveals which taxa such a sample contains, but due to factors such as differing DNA amplification rates and body sizes, its read counts do not neatly correspond to how abundant the different taxa are relative to one another. This lack of relative abundance limits the data's utility for the multitude of ecological analyses that depend on it. We propose BIOTRAM: a neural network that estimates per-taxon specimen counts by dividing the observed read counts by a learned read yield per specimen, which it factors into the DNA each specimen contributes and how efficiently that DNA is amplified. On a paired dataset of 1,188 bottles (800 k specimens) processed both by metabarcoding and by comprehensive individual barcoding for ground-truthing, BIOTRAM reduces the Jensen-Shannon divergence between the estimated and the true composition from 0.3586 for raw read proportions (the usual proxy for abundance) to 0.1200. Trained on the same objective and inputs as four generic deep architectures, all with tuned loss weights, it reaches a count error 3.2% below that of the strongest of them and the lowest composition divergence. It also generalizes to out-of-domain data better, beating all baselines on bottles from unseen regions, later collection dates and unseen sequencing batches, and transferring to data from an unseen laboratory. Structuring the mapping from reads to counts around the steps of the experimental pipeline thus yields more accurate abundance estimates than leaving that mapping unconstrained.

papers.title: Morpheus.AI: agents autonomously generate, execute and refine virtual tissue models
papers.abstract: Virtual tissue models link observations to mechanistic hypotheses, but building them demands expertise in biology, mathematics and programming. Here, large language model (LLM) agents paired with the simulator Morpheus (Morpheus.AI) autonomously built such models from fifteen benchmark studies, five without a published model. With a frontier LLM, agents that ran their simulations met 83-86% of study-specific criteria in under two hours and for under US\$4 per model. Such agents could make in silico modeling routine.

papers.title: Rethinking One Gene, One Token: Transcriptome-Aware Tokenization for Single-Cell Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Single-cell foundation models typically treat each gene as a token, which is both costly and wasteful. A cell can express thousands of genes, so one token per gene makes self-attention expensive, yet many of these genes are detected at low levels and carry too little signal to deserve a token of their own. Genes that are expressed together could instead share a token, leaving separate tokens for genes that stand out. We introduce scTAT (Transcriptome-Aware Tokenization), which pairs a gene-set vocabulary with a per-cell tokenizer. The vocabulary holds overlapping gene sets that recur with stable relative expression across the pretraining corpus. Using these sets raises two difficulties. First, which genes should share a token depends on the cell, whereas existing multi-gene tokens fix the grouping in advance. Second, gene sets of different sizes must be compared with single genes on a common scale. The tokenizer therefore decides per cell, letting gene sets and single genes compete for token positions under an expression score normalized by the square root of set size. Training still reconstructs individual genes, so predictions stay at gene resolution. In frozen-embedding cell-type annotation, scTAT matches the strongest one-gene-per-token model with half the token budget. Its advantage over one-gene-per-token models at the same budget grows as the budget shrinks and the tokenizer assigns more positions to gene sets. Encoding the same genes with gene-set tokens also nearly halves the Transformer's matrix-multiplication cost. These results show that a token need not hold exactly one gene: when the tokenizer decides per cell which genes share a token, a fixed budget covers more of each transcriptome at no cost in annotation accuracy.

papers.title: VenusGenome: Genome-Aware Masked Autoencoding for Microbial Genome Representation Learning
papers.abstract: Genomic-context models have shown that contextualizing protein embeddings can improve predictions of microbial function. We observe that a gene's protein embedding is partially predictable from the embeddings of neighboring genes in the genome, motivating high-ratio masking that requires reconstruction from sparser genomic context. Genomic modeling must also distinguish biological relationships from assembly conventions, since the ordering of separate contigs does not imply adjacency and strand labels depend on the reference orientation. We therefore introduce VenusGenome, a gene-resolution masked autoencoder that combines visible-only encoding with genome-aware attention incorporating contig boundaries, relative strand orientations, and gene positions. We pretrain this model on a curated corpus of over 1.7 million microbial genome assemblies from isolate and metagenomic sources, using frozen protein embeddings as gene-level inputs. Across genome-level phenotype prediction and gene-level tasks, the resulting frozen representations achieve the highest mean performance among the evaluated models on nine of eleven primary metrics. An exploratory gene-input perturbation analysis further links representation sensitivity to experimentally measured fitness defects. Ablations support the contribution of genome-aware attention and show the benefits of masked autoencoding over BERT-style masked modeling, with further gains from higher masking ratios.

papers.title: A Training-Free Socket for DNA in Frozen Language Models
papers.abstract: Connecting a DNA foundation model to a large language model (LLM) usually requires training a connector, and often the LLM too. We show that a closed-form map is enough for gene-level questions. Our method, the socket, fits one ridge regression (the plug) from frozen Evo 2 features to the host LLM's own representation of the gene's symbol, name, and description at an early layer. The plug's output replaces the hidden state at placeholder positions, and no gradient passes through the host. We test it on GeneHop, a five-way multiple-choice benchmark split by homology. In a single run on the held-out test set, under a frozen analysis plan, real DNA beats shuffled DNA on all four hosts: by +22.2 points [19.8, 25.0] on Qwen3.5-4B, +26.1 [24.3, 27.9] on Qwen3.6-27B, +16.7 [14.2, 19.7] on Mistral-7B, and +18.4 [16.2, 21.0] on OLMo-2-7B. All four survive Holm correction, every null control stays within two points of the sham level, and the development results agree within 2.3 points. A layer rule that uses no task items was selected on three hosts; it predicted the working layer of the fourth before any DNA-plug scoring on it. A text-only linear map lets one plug feed any other host, at a cost of at most 0.9 points on test. The socket conveys gene identity: nearest-neighbour retrieval recovers 72-84% of the effect, but the plug beats it on every host by 3.0-5.2 points and keeps most of its effect without training homologs.

papers.title: Deep-Learning Algorithm for Indeterminate Thyroid Nodules: Comparison and Combination with Molecular Testing
papers.abstract: Thyroid nodules with indeterminate cytology (Bethesda III) carry an intermediate risk of malignancy, and molecular testing is widely used to decide between surgery and surveillance, but it is costly and not universally available. We investigated whether a convolutional neural network (CNN) applied to routine ultrasound images can stratify Bethesda III nodules, and how it compares and combines with molecular testing. We retrospectively identified 466 nodule records from 418 patients who underwent molecular testing (Afirma or ThyroSeq). A CNN pre-trained on determinate nodules was adapted to indeterminate nodules with soft labels and transfer learning. After removal of duplicate records, 119 nodules with surgical pathology were used for development and 47 were held out for testing. On the test set, the deep learning (DL) model achieved an AUC of 0.73 (95% CI 0.51-0.94), compared with 0.55 (0.38-0.71) for molecular testing (P = 0.15). At a cut-off inherited from the original algorithm, the DL model was more specific than molecular testing (0.95 vs 0.32; P < 0.001), with a higher positive predictive value (0.67 vs 0.21), a lower sensitivity (0.44 vs 0.78; P = 0.25) and a similar negative predictive value (0.88 vs 0.86). All six DL-positive test nodules were molecular-positive, and the DL output split the molecular-positive nodules into a high-risk (4/6 malignant) and a lower-risk group (3/27 malignant; P = 0.01). Surgical verification was strongly driven by the molecular result (99% of positive vs 19% of negative results), and molecular-test accuracy depended on the platform. A logistic regression of the DL output, nodule size and the molecular result dropped the DL term and did not improve on the DL output alone. Ultrasound DL complemented molecular testing for Bethesda III nodules, in particular by identifying molecular-positive nodules at lower risk of malignancy.

papers.title: AcupunctureBench: A Multimodal Benchmark for Evaluating Generative Models in the Acupuncture Domain
papers.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied in the field of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), standardized benchmark evaluations for TCM have gradually emerged. Acupuncture is a crucial component of TCM. However, existing evaluation benchmarks are lacking in this domain. To address this gap, this paper proposes AcupunctureBench, the first independently constructed large-scale multimodal benchmark for the acupuncture domain, covering text, image, and video modalities. The AcupunctureBench spans multidimen sional knowledge in acupuncture, including acupuncture theory, meridians and acupoints, clinical reasoning, TCM syndromes, and practical acupoint operation. To achieve large-scale construction while ensuring medical professionalism, this work designs a human-machine collaborative data construction pipeline and proposes efficient deduplication strategies to reduce redundant samples, while extensively adopting data synthesis to mitigate data leak age risks. AcupunctureBench contains a total of 58,526 question samples and 1,216 video samples, covering multiple task types including objective questions, subjective question answering, case analysis, image understanding, image reasoning, and video understanding. Based on this benchmark, this paper evaluates 14 large language models, 14 large multimodal models, and 4 video foundation models, and further releases the first dedicated evaluation website for the acupuncture domain.

papers.title: AgentCount: An Agentic Workflow for Traceable Colony Counting and Insight Generation from Agar Plate Images
papers.abstract: Colony counting is commonly used to evaluate microbial populations in food safety testing and microbiological studies. Despite its wide application, manual counting is time-consuming and operator-dependent, and the final count often lacks a record of the objects included in the measurement. To address these limitations, this study presents AgentCount, an open-source agentic workflow for colony counting and result interpretation from agar plate images. Plate photographs and plating metadata are processed through seven agents for image quality control, plate localisation, colony detection, counting, CFU calculation, validation, and reporting. Colony detection is performed using Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM 3) with multiple text prompts and morphology-based filtering. After that, replicate statistics are calculated and a large language model (LLM)-based agent is used to generate a results narrative. Intermediate outputs, including quality scores, segmentation masks, detections, and warnings, are retained to support review of the reported values. The workflow also extends to skill-guided analysis of archived microbial population data. In a retrospective comparison with two previously published studies, we benchmarked 241 published endpoints, including all 216 mean +- SD values of the meat-analogue pathogen tables; on the 168 endpoints with a complete n=6 replicate source, 164 (97.6%) agreed within 0.01 log10 units. Overall, AgentCount demonstrates the promising potential of agentic workflows for applications in applied microbiology.

papers.title: A System One Approach to General Protein Evolution
papers.abstract: Protein engineering requires deciding which mutation to test next and when to stop. Existing approaches often require target-family measurements, encode candidates separately, or return scores that are not calibrated to the assay. We introduce Pev, a general mutation policy that explores a System One approach to protein evolution: learning from experiments across families to make decisions in a single parallel query. Given a parent sequence and an assay context, Pev encodes the parent once and returns calibrated probabilities for choosing an edit or stopping, together with each edit's probability of improving the assay outcome. One policy covers peptides, small folded domains, and antibodies across binding and stability objectives, without fitting model weights to the target family. In ten-well screens on held-out families, Pev finds 3.3$\times$ as many beneficial mutations as random selection and 1.8$\times$ as many as zero-shot ESM-2. It also outperforms a ridge surrogate refitted on target measurements in closed-loop search on the held-out GB1 landscape. Post-hoc calibration improves probability reliability without changing decisions, while shared encoding provides over 800$\times$ the throughput of per-mutant encoding at 1,000 candidates per request. These results suggest that a System One approach could support efficient experimental decisions across protein families, with Pev providing an initial demonstration.

papers.title: A Bayesian Optimized Biquad Filter-Burg Model for Real-Time EEG Phase Estimation
papers.abstract: Real-time phase estimation on stimulus-aligned transient EEG is critical for closed-loop neuromodulation systems targeting the theta-band, yet most real-time phase estimation methods have been developed and validated on resting-state, high-fidelity signals in the alpha band. Recent work has pursued deep learning architectures, while individualized classical bandpass filter tuning remains underexplored. This study characterizes the spectral and temporal properties of non-anticipative bandpass filtering and demonstrates the performance gains achieved through individualized tuning. We present a Bayesian-Optimized Biquad Filter-Burg (BOB) model evaluated on EEG recorded during peripheral vibrotactile stimulation of the left median nerve (theta, N=20 healthy subjects) and on resting-state recordings from the Max Planck Institute's LEMON dataset (alpha, N=20 healthy subjects). BOB was benchmarked against the Deep Dual-Branch Complex Neural Network (DBCNN), EEG Phase Prediction Network (EPN), Phastimate, and Phase Estimation with Autoregressive Padding (PEAP) under matched testing conditions: channel selection, individualized optimization, evaluation time points, and an offline reference phase obtained through zero-phase filtering and the Hilbert transform. Under these testing conditions, BOB achieved matched or better performance than these models at a fraction of the calibration time.

papers.title: A convolution inequality and the Krzy\.z conjecture
papers.abstract: Using a sharp bound for convolutions of non-negative trigonometric polynomials with the Fej\'er kernel resembling a pointwise variant of Bernstein's inequality for polynomials, we prove new properties of extremal functions for the Krzy\.z conjecture. In particular, we resolve a 1993 conjecture of Peretz by showing that if $f$ is extremal for some coefficient, then $|f(0)|\leq 1/e$. Furthermore, we show that if equality holds in this estimate for every extremal function, then the Krzy\.z conjecture is true.

papers.title: Santa Claus and Weighted Nash Social Welfare with Subadditive Valuations
papers.abstract: We study max-min allocation (the Santa Claus problem) and weighted Nash social welfare for $n$ agents with subadditive valuations over $m$ indivisible items. Using demand queries, we give randomized polynomial-time approximation algorithms with factors $O(\sqrt n)$ and $O(\Gamma(w))$, respectively, where $\Gamma(w)=\exp((\ln n-H(w))/2)$ and $H(w)=-\sum_i w_i\ln w_i$ for positive weights summing to one. Both ratios are independent of $m$. The max-min result improves the $2n-1$ bound of Khot and Ponnuswami (2007). We also give simpler $O(\sqrt n)$ algorithms for additive valuations and for submodular valuations with value queries, improving the $O(\sqrt{n\log n})$ bound of Saha and Srinivasan (2018) in the additive case. For Nash welfare, $\Gamma(w)=1$ for equal weights and $\Gamma(w)\le\sqrt n$ in general. We prove a configuration-LP integrality gap of $\Theta(\Gamma(w))$ for every prescribed weight vector, even for XOS valuations. For every fixed $D>0$, we also prove information-theoretic approximation lower bounds of $\Omega_D(\sqrt{n/\ln n})$ and $\Omega_D(\Gamma(w)/\sqrt{\ln n})$, respectively, for randomized algorithms making at most $n^D$ adaptive queries. These hold on XOS instances with $m=\Theta(n)$ items, even with simultaneous access to value, demand, and XOS supporting-clause oracles. They apply both to guarantees with success probability at least $2/3$ and to guarantees in expected welfare. The weighted bound holds for every prescribed weight vector and is vacuous below one. Thus the oracle lower bounds are within an $O(\sqrt{\ln n})$ factor of our upper bounds, while the configuration-LP gaps match them up to constants. Our algorithms build on random matchings for large items and charge the aggregate loss across configurations to the at most $n$ matched items.

papers.title: Hopf algebra polynomial identities in the Sweedler algebra
papers.abstract: Using Mac Lane's PROPs, one can introduce multilinear polynomial identities that involve all the operations of a Hopf algebra: the (co)multiplication, the (co)unit and the antipode. We find bases for polynomial identities and calculate their codimensions for the Sweedler algebra, treating it first as an ordinary associative algebra over a field and second as a Hopf algebra.

papers.title: Constraining tau-sterile neutrino mixing with high-energy astrophysical neutrinos
papers.abstract:
Whether a sterile neutrino mixes with the three active ones remains an open question. Its mixing with the tau neutrino, $|U_{	au 4}|^2$, is the least constrained, since terrestrial experiments probe it only indirectly and over limited ranges of sterile-neutrino mass. We show that TeV-PeV astrophysical neutrinos probe it differently. Their sources make almost no $
u_	au$, but oscillations over cosmological distances turn about one third of them into $
u_	au$ before they reach Earth. Mixing with a sterile neutrino would make these $
u_	au$ scarcer, lowering the $
u_	au$ fraction that neutrino telescopes measure, whatever the sterile-neutrino mass. In contrast, sterile mixing with $
u_e$ or $
u_\mu$ is nearly undetectable. Fitting the flavor composition measured by IceCube, with the composition at the sources left free, we find $|U_{	au 4}|^2 < 0.88$ at 90% C.L. Combining IceCube with present and planned neutrino telescopes, including IceCube-Gen2 and HUNT, could lower this limit to 0.24-0.29 by 2040 and to 0.12-0.14 by 2050. By 2050, these limits would match some present terrestrial limits, though not the strongest.

papers.title: Synthesizing Dexterous Robot Demonstrations from Human Videos via Virtual Try-On
papers.abstract: Robot foundation models have shown remarkable performance in robot control, yet adapting them to a new task still relies heavily on teleoperated demonstrations. Egocentric human videos offer a scalable substitute, but overlaying rendered robots on human videos or retargeting human poses into robot actions leaves significant visual or action gaps for high-DoF robot embodiments. To address this limitation, we propose RoboTryOn, which treats human-to-robot translation as virtual try-on: try-on keeps the person and swaps the garment, RoboTryOn keeps the demonstrated motion and swaps the human for the robot. Specifically, RoboTryOn converts a human video into a video of the target robot specified by a reference image, while preserving the original task, objects, and background. To maintain visual consistency, we translate selected keyframes autoregressively and use them to guide video synthesis with motion conditioned on the human hand skeleton. Additionally, we use an inverse dynamics model (IDM) that incorporates depth features to infer action labels from synthesized videos for policy learning. Our experiments across multiple humanoid embodiments show that policies trained with our synthetic data improve the average success rate on novel tasks, including challenging bimanual manipulation, from 2% to 60%, without any real robot demonstration of those tasks. Moreover, training with our synthetic data matches the performance of policies trained solely on teleoperated demonstrations at approximately a third of the collection cost, demonstrating the cost efficiency of our approach.

papers.title: An elementary proof of a tangent-cone identity for rank-one planar Lipschitz maps
papers.abstract: We give an elementary proof of a tangent-cone identity which might be known to specialists in geometric measure theory. It concerns Lipschitz mappings $g$ from the closed unit ball $B\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ to $\mathbb{R}^2$. Let $x$ be an interior point of differentiability of $g$ at which $Dg(x)$ has rank one. If the upper one-dimensional Hausdorff density of $g(B)$ at $g(x)$ is at most one, then the tangent cone to $g(B)$ at $g(x)$ coincides with the image of $Dg(x)$. This property is used in the proof of rigidity for the four-gradient problem. We provide a detailed, self-contained proof based on differentiability, connectedness and elementary estimates for one-dimensional Hausdorff measure, without using advanced methods from geometric measure theory.

papers.title: Information Loss Is All You Need: $TC^0$ Pseudorandomness from Worst-Case Lattices
papers.abstract: Can deterministic information loss yield post-quantum pseudorandomness with $TC^0$ evaluation? We show that deterministic rounding achieves this under quantum worst-case lattice hardness, with fixed polynomial parameters and no predetermined sample bound. We introduce learning with algebraic rounding (LAR), which applies an explicit integer rounding map to blocks of secret-dependent linear measurements and encodes the result in a lattice quotient. For one fixed family with polynomially bounded modulus and dimensions, deterministic labels on exactly uniform, secret-independent public matrices are computationally indistinguishable from independent uniform labels for every polynomial number of classical random examples. Our classical reduction from Gaussian LWE, combined with the quantum worst-case reduction to LWE, bases LAR on GapSVP and SIVP over general lattices at approximation factor $\widetilde{O}(q)$, where $q$ is the modulus. The proof uses source-independent affine transport: public affine maps sampled independently of the hidden errors transport the Gaussian error law close to uniform on the rounding map's zero-label fiber while preserving exactly uniform public matrices. For every fixed inverse-polynomial accuracy, we give a polynomial-time sampler for the same public parameter family. This yields the first post-quantum weak pseudorandom function with joint key-and-input evaluation in $TC^0$, secure against uniform quantum polynomial-time distinguishers given any polynomial number of classical uniform random examples. We also prove hardness of learning polynomial-size two-hidden-layer ReLU networks from noiseless uniform random examples, even for quantum polynomial-time improper learners.

papers.title: von Neumann Stability Analysis of Braginskii MHD: Thermal Conduction, Viscosity, Magnetic Diffusion, and Thermoelectric Effects; and an Implementation in Athena++
papers.abstract: Athena++ is a finite-volume astrophysical magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) code. As of writing, isotropic thermal conduction and kinematic viscosity, Ohmic resistivity, and ambipolar diffusion are present in the main branch. Here we present a fork of Athena++, ``Athena-Aniso''. It implements fully anisotropic thermal conduction (parallel, perpendicular, and the Righi--Leduc effect); anisotropic viscosity (all five Braginskii viscosity tensors); the Hall effect; and several thermoelectric effects (Peltier, Seebeck, Nernst, and Ettingshausen). These effects can be weighted by ionisation fraction in a partially ionised gas, with the neutral part diffusing isotropically. We have also added isotropic bulk viscosity. The Biermann battery is not implemented here. The dissipative terms have super-time-stepping support, while the non-dissipative terms are combined with the ideal MHD flux. A CFL condition for all terms is derived and implemented using von Neumann stability analysis. The dissipative terms are found to be stable under first-order time integration. The non-dissipative terms are found to be stable under third-order time integration. We additionally derive new signal speeds for a modified HLLE Riemann solver. These suppress grid-scale non-linear instabilities still present in the non-dissipative terms. The Nernst/Ettingshausen system is found to be ill-posed unless it is stabilised by both perpendicular thermal conduction and perpendicular magnetic diffusion. We derive a well-posedness criterion for this. We provide numerical tests of each implemented effect against derived analytical solutions.

papers.title: ScoreDial: Precise Control of Visual Attributes in Image Generation via Regressor Guidance from Limited Human Ratings
papers.abstract: Requested-value control is stricter than continuous steering: given $c$ on a human-rating scale, the generated image should attain that value from only limited ratings. We present ScoreDial, which fits a differentiable regressor $R$ to 100-479 human-rated images; once $R$ is fixed, a requested value $c$ is defined on its output scale, and learned target conditioning is paired with error-adaptive guidance that repeatedly reduces $|R(\mathbf{x})-c|$ during sampling. Across tire slip resistance, interior visual complexity, food desire-to-eat, and soap translucency, using one set of sampler settings, ScoreDial reaches requested values and achieves $R$-MAE at most 0.013 over a range of width 0.8 and Spearman $\rho=0.980$, the maximum attainable under our protocol. Because $R$ also drives sampling, we evaluate agreement with $R$ separately from matched sweeps, an independent auditor fitted to the same ratings on a backbone no deployed regressor uses, and blinded human judgments. MPGD-flow also reaches the requested values under $R$, but ScoreDial has larger auditor displacement on every attribute, the largest among all compared methods, and a stronger MPGD-flow setting gives up target agreement without closing this gap. On every attribute, removing target conditioning leaves low $R$-MAE but more than halves auditor displacement, separating precise score correction from attribute movement. Blinded rating studies with 15 raters per attribute show mean human ratings track $c$ on tire and soap, with linear $R^2=0.665$ and $R^2=0.786$, and in forced-choice comparisons of matched sweeps, raters chose ScoreDial's as the clearer progression in at least 84% of judgments against every baseline. Code: https://github.com/Kamijo-Gen/ScoreDial.

papers.title: Unifying and Beyond the Theory of Pervasive Capability Degradation in LLM Post-training SFT from Feature Interference
papers.abstract: Pervasive Capability Degradation (PCD) refers to the phenomenon in which supervised fine-tuning (SFT), while adapting a large language model (LLM) to a target task, often erodes the general capabilities acquired during pre-training. Prevailing explanations attribute PCD to macroscopic distribution shift and therefore lack microscopic manipulability, leaving existing mitigation methods without a complete theoretical foundation. In this paper, we first develop a bottom-up geometric theory of PCD grounded in feature interference under superposition: narrow-domain SFT data disrupt the almost-orthogonal feature structure formed during pre-training, and the resulting interference drives activations across decision hyperplanes in the output Laguerre-Voronoi geometry, flipping predictions on general tasks. This theory unifies existing methods into six paradigms and reveals both the source of their efficacy and their limitations. We then argue that cross-entropy under one-hot supervision is structurally limited in resolving PCD on its own, and accordingly propose the AEGIS loss, which directly constrains the drift of activation margins along all competing token directions, thereby decoupling interference suppression from task adaptation. Across 3 model families and 14 SFT tasks, AEGIS outperforms representative methods of every paradigm on target tasks and pervasive capabilities simultaneously, at only about 1.3 times the computational cost of standard SFT. Its generality, scalability, and mechanistic interpretability offer a new perspective on mitigating PCD.

papers.title: Modeling runaway electron mitigation via passively driven plasma instabilities in a high-current tokamak
papers.abstract: A critical challenge for tokamak-based fusion power plants is the formation of high-current, relativistic runaway electron (RE) beams during abrupt confinement loss events called disruptions. RE beams may significantly damage machine components if left unmitigated, jeopardizing the operational and economic viability of fusion power plants. We present the first self-consistent extended magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) computational study of RE mitigation with a passively driven RE mitigation coil (REMC) in a high-current tokamak. RE generation and transport are coupled with REMC-driven MHD activity in a 3D simulation that models the thermal and current quench phases of a mid-plane disruption, together with the vertical displacement and final termination of the plasma and RE beam on SPARC -- a high-field, high-current tokamak designed to achieve a fusion gain Q > 1. We demonstrate that REMC-driven magnetic stochasticity can reduce the RE current by over an order-of-magnitude when compared to unmitigated disruptions. The final termination is mediated via a post-thermal-quench "cold" vertical displacement of the plasma, which, together with magnetic stochasticity, increases RE losses via scrape-off once the plasma contacts the first wall. These results demonstrate a viable mechanism for RE mitigation using passively driven plasma instabilities on high-current tokamaks.

papers.title: Study of enhancing the signal-background separation for the Higgs boson production in association with a single top-quark in $pp$ collisions at the LHC
papers.abstract: In this paper, a multivariate analysis based approach for enhancing the extraction of the rare Standard Model (SM) process being studied - Higgs boson production in association with a single top quark (tH) - from the prevailing background processes is presented. The analysis was performed using a Monte Carlo generated dataset simulating the outcomes of proton-proton collisions at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). A deep fully connected neural network was developed for signal-background discrimination, incorporating a masking mechanism designed to suppress the contribution of input variables associated with objects that were not reconstructed in a given event. The performance of the masked architecture was evaluated on independent Monte Carlo samples. The results of the proposed methodology are compared with a conventional cut-based approach in terms of the statistical significance of the tH production channel. The developed framework was tested using a simulated dataset corresponding approximately to the combined statistical samples of LHC Runs 1, 2, and 3.

papers.title: Relative Tate-Shafarevich kernel of a reductive group over a global field
papers.abstract: We describe an algorithm and a computer program computing the relative Tate-Shafarevich kernel $Sha^S(K,G)$ of a reductive group $G$ over a global field $K$ with respect to a finite set $S$ of places of $K$ containing no archimedean places. We assume that we know the algebraic fundamental group $\Lambda=\pi_1^{alg}(G)$ together with the action on it of the Galois group $\Theta=Gal(L/K)$, where $L/K$ is a finite Galois extension with no real places such that $Gal(K^s/L)$ acts trivially on $\Lambda$. We also assume that we know the decomposition subgroups $\Theta_v\subseteq \Theta$ for all places $v$ in $S$, and all non-cyclic decomposition subgroups $\Theta_v$ for $v$ outside $S$. Under certain conditions, we compute the set $Sha^S(K,G)$ also when $S$ contains archimedean places.

papers.title: Precise and accurate nuclear electric quadrupole moment of $^{223}$Ra from molecular spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Nuclear electric quadrupole moments of unstable isotopes are commonly extracted from laser spectroscopy of the atomic hyperfine structure, where the accuracy is limited to the several-percent level by the available electric-field-gradient (EFG) calculations. In this study, we determine the spectroscopic quadrupole moment of $^{223}$Ra (half-life $t_{1/2} = 11.4$ d) from hyperfine-resolved collinear resonance ionization spectroscopy of the radioactive molecule $^{223}$Ra$^{19}$F. The $X\,^2\Sigma^+$ electronic ground state of RaF provides a large axial EFG at the radium nucleus that can be calculated with relativistic coupled-cluster theory to sub-percent accuracy. Together with a three-fold improvement in spectral resolution over previous fast-beam measurements of radioactive molecules, this yields $Q_s = +1.211(7)_\mathrm{stat}(2)_\mathrm{syst}(5)_\mathrm{theo}\,e\mathrm{b}$ for $^{223}$Ra with a total uncertainty of 0.73%, approximately three times better than atomic and ionic determinations. This result demonstrates that molecular spectroscopy can provide access to the electromagnetic structure of unstable nuclei with a precision competitive with, and in favorable cases better than, atomic spectroscopy, and may thus be envisioned for studies beyond the limitations of current radioactive-atom experiments.

papers.title: Decentralized Sparse Quantile Regression
papers.abstract: Distributed statistical learning has recently attracted significant attention owing to its computational efficiency and scalability in large-scale systems. However, the non-smooth quantile loss poses substantial challenges to the development of efficient decentralized algorithms for quantile regression. Existing methods may either suffer from slow convergence or rely on smoothing-based approximations that require additional stringent assumptions, particularly in high-dimensional settings. To address these issues, we propose a decentralized framework that integrates gradient tracking with iterative hard thresholding for sparse quantile estimation. The proposed method avoids smoothing approximations and relaxes the initialization requirement. Theoretically, we show that the proposed algorithm achieves linear convergence under stated regularity conditions and that the resulting estimator attains the same order of statistical accuracy as its centralized counterpart. We further develop a decentralized information criterion for selecting the working sparsity level and establish support screening guarantees. Numerical experiments and a real-data study illustrate the finite-sample performance of the proposed method.

papers.title: Light Mediators at the Neutrino-Dark Matter Frontier: Coherent Scattering, Precision Constraints, and Complementary Searches
papers.abstract: Low-threshold neutrino and dark-matter experiments constrain light mediators through different momentum transfers, targets, and coupling combinations. We examine scalar and vector interactions in coherent neutrino--nucleus scattering, neutrino--electron scattering, and dark-matter direct detection. Three representative interaction models are used to compare recoil spectra and coupling degeneracies. For $^{73}\mathrm{Ge}$ and $^{131}\mathrm{Xe}$, the nuclear-charge response matrix has a condition number of approximately 115, so two different targets may still leave nearly parallel blind directions. An analytic profile-likelihood calculation shows how spectral overlap and uncertainties in neutrino interactions affect dark-matter discovery sensitivity in the neutrino fog. We discuss the implications of measurements from COHERENT, CONUS+, LZ, XENONnT, and PandaX-4T and specify which theoretical inputs, detector responses, and statistical correlations are needed to combine their constraints. keyword : coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering; light mediators; neutrino--electron scattering; dark matter direct detection; non-standard interactions; solar neutrinos; complementarity

papers.title: Reflective algebras over factorizable Hopf algebras
papers.abstract: The reflective algebra $(R_H(A),K_{\mathrm{ref}}(A))$, introduced by Laugwitz, Walton and Yakimov, is a quasitriangular left $H$-comodule algebra constructed from a quasitriangular Hopf algebra $(H,R)$ and a left $H$-comodule algebra $A$. We study the structure and factorizability of finite-dimensional reflective algebras. When $(H,R)$ is factorizable, we show that $(R_H(A),K_{\mathrm{ref}}(A))$ is isomorphic, as a quasitriangular left $H$-comodule algebra, to $A\otimes H$ equipped with the trivial left $H$-coaction on $A$ and the universal $K$-matrix induced by $R_{21}R$. In this case, we also classify all universal $K$-matrices on $R_H(A)$. Finally, we prove that $(R_H(A),K_{\mathrm{ref}}(A))$ is factorizable if and only if $(H,R)$ is factorizable and $A$ is simple as an algebra.

papers.title: Predicting protein structures at any folding stage from sequence
papers.abstract: Protein structure prediction has largely focused on native conformations, leaving the continuum of unfolded states, folding intermediates, and native structures difficult to access. We present FoldScape, a sequence-conditioned deep learning framework for generating protein conformational ensembles at specified folding fractions $Q$. Trained on approximately one million conformations from 10,000 protein sequences, FoldScape combines coarse-grained folding and all-atom mechanical-unfolding trajectories. It reconstructs three-dimensional $C_\alpha$ chains through hierarchical sliding-window regressions of inter-residue distances, chain-level assembly, and a rectified-flow decoder. By conditioning on folding progress, FoldScape generates conformations from unfolded states through intermediates to native-state structures without protein-specific molecular dynamics at inference. In matched-sample comparisons, FoldScape achieves median conformational-space coverage of 0.989, 0.722, and 0.877 along radius of gyration, fraction of native contacts $Q$, and secondary-structure fraction, respectively, versus 0.05, 0.05, and 0.10 for seed-varied AlphaFold 3 ensembles. Coverage advantages are consistent across the evaluated proteins and robust to binning choices. Reconstruction accuracy remains approximately stable across the evaluated stages of a folding trajectory, and stride-one crop-and-superpose inference extends predictions to chains several times longer than the single-pass limit. Analyses of mechanical-unfolding trajectories show residue-resolved pathways, reproducible extension-conditioned observables across pulling velocities, and geometrically coherent segments in partially unfolded chains. FoldScape extends sequence-based structure prediction beyond a single folded endpoint to controllable conformational-ensemble generation across protein folding.

papers.title: Galois-modular obstructions to the categorification of near-group fusion rings
papers.abstract: In this article we establish new obstructions to the categorification of near-group fusion rings by combining the values of irreducible characters of the Grothendieck ring with the Galois symmetry of the induced unit object $I(1)$ in the Drinfeld center. As a result, we show that a near-group ring of type $G+m$, where $G$ is an abelian group and both $|G|$ and $m$ are odd, can only categorify if $m=|G|$.

papers.title: LiSA: Linear Stochastic Attention for Long-Range Visual Modeling
papers.abstract: Self-attention has become the standard for modern sequence modeling, enabling Transformers to model long-range dependencies across a wide range of modalities. Despite these advances, its quadratic cost with respect to sequence length remains a significant computational bottleneck. Recent work addresses this limitation by introducing linear variants of self-attention, namely with kernel approximations of the softmax operator. However, their first-order aggregation restricts expressivity and struggles to capture higher-order structure. We propose Linear Stochastic Attention (LiSA), a linear attention plug-in module that enables higher-order token interactions via a stochastic diffusion process based on truncated random walks. LiSA incorporates adaptive locality, favoring semantically similar neighbors to preserve fine-grained structures, while maintaining stable and efficient training. We conduct extensive experiments on classification, semantic segmentation, and object detection tasks and show improved results over state-of-the-art methods.

papers.title: P$^2$-MOPD: Accelerating Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation via Parameter Priors
papers.abstract: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation consolidates expert capabilities by supervising student-generated trajectories, whereas task arithmetic offers a training-free alternative through linear parameter combinations. We view the linear combination of student and expert parameters as a single differentiable model and propose P$^2$-MOPD, which jointly optimizes the mixing coefficients and the student weights under the same on-policy distillation objective. Unlike task arithmetic, which stays within the span of the frozen student and expert parameters for any choice of merging coefficients, P$^2$-MOPD keeps the student trainable, so the experts act as parameter priors without confining it to this span. Across four domains at 1.7B and 4B scales, P$^2$-MOPD achieves faster and more balanced recovery than MOPD from the same initialization, surpassing its final average recovery in half the training steps. At the end of training, our 1.7B model reaches 94.7% average recovery, versus 80.9% for MOPD.

papers.title: Contrast-Enhanced Nonlinear Imaging with Moir\'e Flatband Superlattices
papers.abstract: Nonlinear metasurfaces offer a compact platform for infrared-to-visible conversion and imaging, yet resonant enhancement is often accompanied by restricted angular acceptance, limiting the range of transverse spatial frequencies that can interact efficiently with the nonlinear modes. Here, we address this challenge using a one-dimensional photonic moir\'e superlattice supporting multiple quasi-flat bands in the near-infrared. These moir\'e modes combine strong near-field enhancement with broad momentum-space accessibility, enabling efficient third-harmonic generation (THG) while maintaining stable excitation over a large angular range. Experimentally, we observe strong THG emission near $467~\mathrm{nm}$ under broadband excitation from $ 1180$ to $ 2000~\mathrm {nm} $. We further employ the nonlinear moir\'e superlattice for infrared imaging by converting an infrared target into visible through the THG process. By encoding image information into displacement-dependent THG signals and decoding their spatial variations, we experimentally resolve weak features and internal textures with improved contrast compared with THG imaging using nonlinear films or conventional nonlinear metasurfaces. These results establish photonic moir\'e superlattices as a versatile platform combining efficient frequency conversion, broad angular acceptance, and mode-sensitive spatial encoding for high-contrast, label-free nonlinear imaging with enhanced feature discrimination.

papers.title: FADE: Factored Ability--Difficulty Filtering for Online RLVR Scheduling
papers.abstract: Group-based reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) learns only from prompts whose sampled completions disagree: all-pass and all-fail groups produce zero relative advantage and burn generation budget without moving the policy. Adaptive schedulers try to steer rollouts toward informative prompts, yet they rely on per-prompt pass-rate trackers that entangle two quantities evolving at very different speeds---the policy's shifting competence across reasoning skills and each prompt's intrinsic difficulty. When a single exponential average or Beta counter tracks both at once, short memory scrambles the relative ordering of prompts whereas long memory reports stale pass rates. We introduce FADE (Factored Ability--Difficulty Estimation), a bilinear state-space filter that separates the two timescales. FADE represents each prompt's success logit as the inner product of a whitened $K$-dimensional skill loading with a fast-drifting policy ability vector, minus a slow-shrinking scalar item intercept. Using P\'olya--Gamma augmentation, each minibatch of binary rollout outcomes updates the $K$-dimensional ability posterior in closed form via a rank-$K$ Woodbury step, instantly transferring competence shifts to all unobserved prompts that share those skills while leaving item intercepts stable. From the resulting posterior mean and variance we derive a closed-form utility for the probability of drawing a non-degenerate rollout group. Across five reasoning benchmarks, two base models, and four scheduling paradigms under a matched rollout budget, FADE consistently improves downstream accuracy and calibration while adding less than $0.6$\,ms per step.

papers.title: Sonar-MoE: In-Backward Expert Updates for Memory-Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Training
papers.abstract: Most parameters of a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model belong to its experts, and standard training keeps every expert gradient in GPU memory until the optimizer step. This memory grows with the number and size of the experts, so it rises as MoE models scale. We introduce Sonar-MoE, which updates each expert tensor during the backward pass and frees its gradient right away. It brings optimizer-in-backward from dense models to batched MoE expert tensors, so the GPU never holds more than one layer of expert gradients. When we fine-tune OLMoE-1B-7B and Granite-3.1-3B-A800M in bf16 with two expert-kernel backends, Sonar-MoE lowers peak memory by 19% to 22%. Its updates are bitwise identical to standard training without expert gradient clipping, and held-out loss stays within 0.003 of all baselines. Each step also takes 17% to 23% less time than standard training with global-norm clipping. Updating whole batched tensors rather than individual experts is what keeps Sonar-MoE fast, as it avoids a 20% to 72% slowdown while using the same memory. Sonar-MoE matches optimizer-in-backward over all parameters in memory and speed while still clipping the dense parameters.

papers.title: Gaussian Matrices and Exterior Forms: Deterministic Principal Ideals
papers.abstract: For an infinite Gaussian matrix with independent entries and doubly monotone variances, we identify its algebraic principal ideal by a deterministic shell profile. The exact boundedness condition also implies compactness. A lower singular-value estimate uniform in the mean gives an exact sum law under each fixed compact perturbation. Conditional products and spatial compression yield the corresponding classification for Gaussian evaluations of Hilbert two-forms. For Wiener area of covariance rank at least two, the generator is the covariance tail divided by its index. The area and covariance generate the same ideal precisely under regularity at infinity.

papers.title: Exact Agreement Expansion up to the Top via Non-polarity
papers.abstract: Agreement expansion asks whether local assignments to faces of a poset that usually agree on a sampled common face must agree with a single global function on most faces. Agreement expansion is exact (approximate) if local assignments need to exactly (approximately) agree with the global function. We suggest a new proof technique for agreement expansion that enables agreement expansion in settings which were previously beyond reach, such as: exact agreement expansion for Grassmannian posets (before only simplicial complexes support exact agreement expansion); agreement expansion based on assignments to top faces of the a complex (before agreement expansion is generally proven only for assignments to low dimensional faces); agreement expansion from one-sided spectral expansion (before, two sided spectral assumption was needed in general settings). Specifically, for down-closed simplicial and Grassmannian complexes, we prove an exact agreement theorem between any two layers assuming one-sided spectral expansion in links of singletons. As an application, we show that full bases of every rank-$k$ matroid admit exact agreement with soundness $O(k^2/[h(k-h)])$ when tested through $h$-element independent sets. We also obtain exact agreement on Grassmannian posets under one-sided spectral expansion, with stronger soundness under a local distance guarantee. Our key proof ideas center around non-polarity of the distributions of local assignments, probed via a random exposure of elements.

papers.title: The strong fractional choice number can exceed the choice number by an arbitrarily large amount
papers.abstract: Erd\H{o}s, Rubin and Taylor asked whether $(a,b)$-choosability implies $(am,bm)$-choosability for all positive integers $a,b,m$. Dvo\v{r}\'ak, Hu and Sereni disproved this for $(a,b,m)=(4,1,2)$ and asked whether a $3$-choosable graph can fail to be $(6,2)$-choosable. Following Jiang and Zhu, Li and Zhu asked whether every $k$-choosable graph is $(kb+1,b)$-choosable for all positive integers $k,b$. Equivalently, Xu and Zhu asked whether $\operatorname{ch}_f^s(G)\le\operatorname{ch}(G)$ for every graph $G$. Here $\operatorname{ch}(G)$ is the choice number, and $\operatorname{ch}_f^s(G)$ is the strong fractional choice number, defined as the infimum of real $r$ such that $G$ is $(a,b)$-choosable for all positive integers $a,b$ with $a/b\ge r$. We prove that, for all integers $t\ge0$ and $b\ge7t+2$, there is a planar graph $G$ with $\operatorname{ch}(G)=3$ that is not $(3b+t,b)$-choosable. This answers all these questions and gives a lower bound of $1/7$ on the supremum of $\operatorname{ch}_f^s(G)-\operatorname{ch}(G)$ over planar graphs of choice number three. For all integers $k\ge4$, $t\ge0$ and $b\ge3t+2$, we construct a graph $G$ with $\operatorname{ch}(G)=k$ that is not $(kb+t,b)$-choosable, using the six-vertex wheel $W_5$ as its core gadget. This gives the corresponding lower bound $1/3$ for each $k\ge4$. The case $t=0$ and $b=2$ recovers the main result of Dvo\v{r}\'ak, Hu and Sereni. Finally, for every integer $t\ge1$, there are a positive integer $k$ and a $k$-choosable graph that is not $(8k+4t-1,8)$-choosable. Thus the difference between the strong fractional choice number and the choice number is unbounded, even with multiplicity fixed at eight. We further prove $k+\Omega(\log k)\le\sup\{\operatorname{ch}_f^s(G):\operatorname{ch}(G)=k\}\le2^{(1+o(1))k}$ as $k$ tends to infinity.

papers.title: Hodge--Riemann relations for $m$-positive and generalized $m$-positive forms
papers.abstract: We study Hodge--Riemann relations for ordinary, sequential, and weak $m$-positive real $(1,1)$-forms in complex dimension $d$. For ordinary $m$-positive forms, we prove the fully mixed relations in every permitted bidegree without assuming semipositivity, generalizing results by Xiao. As a generalization of ordinary $m$-positivity, sequential $m$-positivity is defined by the hyperbolicity cones of successive directional derivatives of the determinant. We formulate a generalized mixed Hodge--Riemann conjecture for this condition and prove several cases beyond the scalar inequalities supplied by hyperbolicity. We prove strict strong positivity for good prefixes with at most three repeated blocks after the first factor. We also consider weak $m$-positivity which corresponds to the pointwise subsolution condition for the complex $m$-Hessian equation. In this setting, we prove the Hodge--Riemann relations for $p\neq q$ and in several diagonal cases, and show that the associated power map induces a pointwise diffeomorphism onto the cone of positive $(d-1,d-1)$-forms. Using Dinh and Nguy\^en's $L^2$ globalization method, we pass from the pointwise relations to cohomology classes on compact K\"ahler manifolds. Finally, we propose conjectures on a numerical criterion for sequential $m$-positive classes and on the solvability of the generalized $m$-Hessian equation.

papers.title: The kinetic Kato square root problem
papers.abstract: We solve the kinetic Kato square root problem for the whole-space Kolmogorov operator $$H_A=\partial_t-X\cdot\nabla_Y-\operatorname{div}_X(A\nabla_X)$$ on \(\mathrm L^2\) with Lebesgue measure, where \(A\) is a bounded measurable complex uniformly accretive matrix depending on all variables. We define its realization through a sesquilinear form and identify the square-root domains of the resulting maximal accretive operator and its adjoint with the intrinsic Sobolev space defined by one velocity derivative and half a derivative along the transport flow. The homogeneous norm equivalences depend only on the dimension and the coefficient bounds. The energy also controls a position derivative of order one third. The proof uses second-order resolvents and localized affine testing. A regularized transport symmetrizer gives hidden coercivity, while comparison with a positive Rockland operator supplies intrinsic smoothing. Commutator and dyadic approximation estimates remove the smoothing before a Carleson argument is applied. We also obtain uniform shifted square-root estimates and bounded velocity, transport and position Riesz transforms.

papers.title: Machine-learning discovery potential for a heavy Higgs boson in $e^+e^-\to ZH$ at a future lepton collider
papers.abstract:
A study of the discovery potential for a CP-even heavy neutral Higgs boson $H$ is presented in the Type-I two-Higgs-doublet model (2HDM) at a future $e^+e^-$ collider with $\sqrt{s}=500~\mathrm{GeV}$, focusing on the process $e^+e^-	o ZH$ with $H	o WW$, and with $Z	o\ell\ell$ or $Z	o
u
u$. The final states are four jets plus two leptons ($4j2\ell$) and four jets plus missing transverse momentum ($4j2
u$). Both a Boosted Decision Tree (BDT) and a Deep Neural Network (DNN) were trained on the same inputs. The BDT was found to be substantially faster in training and inference without any loss of performance, and it is therefore the classifier used in the interpretation. Three strategies are compared: a cut-based analysis, a one-dimensional BDT selection trained per mass point, and a two-dimensional (BDT $	imes$ $m_H$) template analysed with a profile likelihood. The 2D template improves the expected discovery significance by a factor of $2.5$--$3.6$ in the $4j2\ell$ channel and by a factor of $5$--$18$ in the $4j2
u$ channel relative to the cut-based analysis, with the largest gains at high $m_H$ where the cut-based mass window loses efficiency. We translate the expected exclusions into $95\%$ CL upper limits on $\sigma 	imes$ BR and discuss the implications for the Type-I 2HDM parameter space.

papers.title: eigenkit: A Provider-Neutral Quantum Computing Library
papers.abstract: Quantum software ecosystems provide increasingly capable tools for simulation and hardware execution, but differences in programming models, supported features, and backend capabilities can make it difficult to move and systematically compare the same quantum algorithm across execution environments. We introduce eigenkit, a provider-neutral quantum computing library that separates algorithm definition from backend execution through a common circuit representation and provider interface. The library currently supports 12 execution providers spanning simulators and quantum hardware, provides backend-independent gradient computation, and integrates with standard scientific-computing and machine-learning workflows through NumPy, PyTorch, and scikit-learn interfaces. We evaluate the practical relevance of this abstraction across both simulation and quantum hardware. Simulator performance varies substantially with circuit size, structure, batching, and application workload, showing that no single backend is consistently preferable. On quantum hardware, experiments on IBM Heron and IQM Emerald show that which processor is better suited to a given algorithm depends not only on hardware constraints, but also on how well the topology of the quantum algorithm matches the physical connectivity of the processor. These results demonstrate that backend portability is not only a software-design convenience, but can be important for both computational efficiency and quantum execution quality.

papers.title: TailorRig: Controllable and Structured Auxiliary Skeleton Generation for Garment-Aware Rigging
papers.abstract: Humanoid rigging for modern characters with complex garments remains challenging due to the need for dense auxiliary skeletons and precise skinning control. Existing automatic methods primarily recover rigs from geometry, providing limited artist control over auxiliary articulation and often lacking explicit semantic or kinematic-chain structure for dense garment bones, leading to instability and weight bleeding. We present TailorRig, a framework that reformulates garment-aware humanoid rigging as a structured, controllable full-rig generation problem. This formulation shifts the goal from automatic rig recovery to artist-driven rig authoring, where both body-template compatibility and auxiliary articulation are explicit design choices. TailorRig exposes two explicit axes of artist control within a unified framework: a user-specified body skeleton template that preserves body-rig compatibility, and artist-provided semantic labels that drive an autoregressive generator to synthesize requested category-specific auxiliary bone chains.
